Hi Alyssa / Tom —

Thanks again for the renewal signal this week — excited to keep BrightLayer on the platform. I wanted to kick off a short renewal coordination thread to align on two things before we lock paperwork: a) the term/price tradeoffs we discussed, and b) the capacity uplift (burst pool + reserved baseline) you mentioned in the call.

Proposed first steps (we can adjust based on your team):
- Quick QBR (30–45m) to review last 12 months usage, finalize capacity targets, and agree on pricing/term tradeoffs.
- We’ll circulate a Mutual Action Plan (attached) with milestones: usage export, legal review window, PO/DocuSign, and go-live for capacity uplift.
- Security package: short SOC2 summary attached; if you need the full report we can route that to procurement.

Suggested QBR windows (PT):
- Thurs Jan 15: 09:00–09:45 or 14:00–14:45
- Fri Jan 16: 11:00–11:45

Requests for you before the QBR:
- Can procurement confirm target billing cadence (monthly vs. quarterly)?
- Can you pull a 6–12 month token-volume export (simple CSV) for the accounts that will be on the uplift? David / Marissa can give the schema.

I’ve attached the MAP and SOC2 summary for convenience. If any of these times work, I’ll send a calendar invite and a brief agenda.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz

Hi all —

Thanks for the quick reply — holding Thurs 1/15 14:00 PT for now. I pulled together two compact pricing scenarios (we’ll send a one-page delta during the QBR):

Scenario A — 24 months, 10% discount vs list, reserved baseline sized to 80% of median sustained load + 25% burst buffer. Ideal if you want predictable unit costs and fewer admin changes mid-term.

Scenario B — 12 months, 5% discount vs list, higher per-token rate but includes flexible mid-term conversion credits if you convert to reserved capacity within 6 months. Better if you want flexibility while you validate spike patterns.

Operational notes we’ll cover in the QBR:
- Latency targets (us-west): reserved baseline 95th percentile < 200ms; burst pool P95 ≈ 350ms (depends on sequence length and model).
- Autoscale warmup: plan for a 3–6 minute ramp for large batch bursts; we can provide a prefetched KV cache option to reduce cold-warm latency for frequent prefixes.

Action items for the QBR prep:
- Alyssa / BrightLayer: usage export (6–12 months) — CSV schema: account_id, date, tokens_in, tokens_out, model, avg_seq_len. Marissa will attach the schema to the calendar invite.
- Redwood: we’ll bring a short delta sheet + an SRE readout (latency percentiles).

I’ve attached an initial pricing delta sheet and the MAP (same file Vanessa sent) for reference.

Thanks —
David Kim
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Attachments: BL_pricing_delta_v1.xlsx (xlsx, 22KB)
